title: Cloud restore bypasses the safe database restore lifecycle
body:
<!-- omera-review-2026-10-05:R01 -->

## Summary and actual behavior

**Reproduced and code-confirmed.** [cloud_backup.rs:903](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/cloud_backup.rs#L903) makes a raw rollback copy of only the live main database, ignores backup errors, and copies the restored file directly over the active database. [commands.rs:4739](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/commands.rs#L4739) calls this while `AppState` and workers still hold database connections; restart occurs only afterward. The database enables a 256 MB mmap at [db.rs:177](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/crates/omera-storage/src/db.rs#L177).

With a synthetic active WAL connection, this Windows build fails with `Failed to replace live database ... user-mapped section open (os error 1224)`. No real database was restored. On systems allowing the copy, the source path still has active connections/WAL and non-atomic replacement risk; corruption or WAL contamination was not demonstrated on this host. Local restore already uses `recovery::stage_restore`, so cloud restore should use the same lifecycle.

## Environment and evidence

- Baseline: Omera 0.4.3, `dev` at [`bdac8fb`](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/commit/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5); SQLite schema 15.
- Review host: Windows; the inspected application was launched from the repository root with `pnpm run tauri dev`.
- Evidence strength is stated above. For code-confirmed scenarios, the steps below describe a targeted validation scenario rather than a completed end-to-end reproduction. Remote-provider, destructive real-library and cross-platform scenarios were not exercised.

## Reproduction or validation scenario

1. Create a temporary SQLite database using `Database::connect`, leaving its WAL-enabled connection open.
2. Create a different snapshot using `create_cloud_snapshot` with the LocalPath provider.
3. Call `restore_cloud_snapshot` for the active path while the first connection is alive.

## Expected behavior

Restore is staged and activated before opening SQLite connections; the current database remains recoverable on failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use the existing staged restore lifecycle and activate before connections/workers start.
- [ ] Validate integrity, schema and foreign keys; create a consistent, verified rollback snapshot.
- [ ] Test active WAL, Windows mmap, interrupted activation, failed rollback creation and restart recovery.

## Related work and scope

Related closed issues: #98. This report describes the remaining behavior on the baseline above and does not assume that every earlier fix is absent.

Implementation must respect the lead-owned persistence, file-safety, migration or update-trust boundaries in [ENGINEERING_HANDOFF.md](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/docs/ENGINEERING_HANDOFF.md). title: Pipeline harvesting can overwrite a different existing asset
body:
<!-- omera-review-2026-10-05:R02 -->

## Summary and actual behavior

**Code-confirmed.** [commands.rs:4250](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/commands.rs#L4250) considers an existing destination with the same basename and byte length already ingested; equal length does not establish identical content. If lengths differ, [commands.rs:4258](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/commands.rs#L4258) calls `fs::copy` onto the existing file, silently overwriting it. The `.txt` sidecar has the same overwrite behavior. A subsequent upsert can associate the replacement with the original record and its organization.

Reproduction condition: two generators produce distinct `output.png` files into a pipeline whose managed destination already contains that name. Fix through a common no-clobber publication service, explicit collision policy, content verification, and per-item receipts. 

The plain managed-import fallback at [commands.rs:884](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/commands.rs#L884) also assumes that same basename plus equal byte length means identical content. It reuses the existing file/record instead of copying a distinct equal-length asset. This path renames differing-length collisions, so its defect is silent false deduplication rather than the pipeline's overwrite behavior. Include both import paths in the collision acceptance tests.

## Environment and evidence

- Baseline: Omera 0.4.3, `dev` at [`bdac8fb`](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/commit/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5); SQLite schema 15.
- Review host: Windows; the inspected application was launched from the repository root with `pnpm run tauri dev`.
- Evidence strength is stated above. For code-confirmed scenarios, the steps below describe a targeted validation scenario rather than a completed end-to-end reproduction. Remote-provider, destructive real-library and cross-platform scenarios were not exercised.

## Reproduction or validation scenario

1. Use synthetic source and managed pipeline folders; place different valid images named `output.png` in each.
2. Run the manual pipeline harvest with different source/destination byte lengths.
3. Repeat with distinct equal-length files, then with plain managed import; include `.txt` sidecars.

## Expected behavior

Distinct content is preserved under distinct destination names; deduplication requires content identity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use no-clobber publication for assets and sidecars across pipeline and plain managed import.
- [ ] Verify content before reusing an existing file or ID; do not infer identity from byte length.
- [ ] Test different-size collisions, equal-size different content, identical content, partial publication and retry.

title: Deferred pipeline cleanup does not revalidate the destination or source identity
body:
<!-- omera-review-2026-10-05:R03 -->

## Summary and actual behavior

**Code-confirmed.** [commands.rs:4331](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/commands.rs#L4331) trashes the queued source pathname once its deadline arrives. It does not use `target_file_id` to check that the managed copy still exists and matches, or verify that the source pathname still represents the file originally ingested. Cleanup is invoked during application startup.

If the destination disappears before the grace period ends, cleanup can remove the remaining original. If a generator replaces the source with a new file at the same path, cleanup can remove that newer file instead.

## Environment and evidence

- Baseline: Omera 0.4.3, `dev` at [`bdac8fb`](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/commit/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5); SQLite schema 15.

Cleanup preserves a source unless the verified managed destination exists and the source still matches the ingested item.

title: Legacy configuration migration can fail and still be recorded as successful
body:
<!-- omera-review-2026-10-05:R04 -->

## Summary and actual behavior

**Code-confirmed.** [legacy_migration.rs:254](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/legacy_migration.rs#L254) loads the legacy config and ignores both credential migration and destination save errors. [config_store.rs:99](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/config_store.rs#L99) rejects saving a nonzero legacy revision into an absent destination whose default revision is zero. The coordinator still appends a `config` artifact with status `success` even when no destination config exists.

Additionally, `config_store::load` may rewrite the legacy source to protect plaintext secrets, so this supposedly source-preserving migration reads through a mutating API. Cleanup preview at [legacy_migration.rs:389](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/legacy_migration.rs#L389) marks config and models eligible after checking database health, without validating those destination artifacts. Current Vue code has no cleanup consumer, so cleanup exposure is latent; the migration false-success path itself is active.

## Environment and evidence

- Baseline: Omera 0.4.3, `dev` at [`bdac8fb`](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/commit/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5); SQLite schema 15.

1. Prepare a supported legacy config with a nonzero revision and no Omera destination config.
2. Invoke the legacy migration coordinator; compare its receipt with the destination configuration.
3. Inspect whether reading the legacy config changes its bytes, and whether cleanup eligibility validates config/model destinations.

## Expected behavior

Migration is source-preserving, reports every failed artifact accurately and permits cleanup only after artifact-specific destination validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Read legacy config without mutating the source and handle revisions explicitly during migration.
- [ ] Propagate credential/save errors and verify destination artifacts before recording success.

<!-- omera-review-2026-10-05:R07 -->
